candidates.demonstrated_gap: Neither winner executes Pine source: NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5/rc6 and LEAN 985ef30 only run ported code, so task T16 has no independent reference that runs the original .pine strategy on our own bars. PineTS is the only maintained runtime found that transpiles native Pine v5 and v6 .pine source offline (v6 marked experimental upstream) from a supplied OHLCV array, with no data provider or service. It also implements strategy(process_orders_on_close=true) for market orders, filling them at the bar close. That matches NautilusTrader's documented default: an order submitted from on_bar settles against the book left at bar N's close, and the engine has no native next-bar-open fill mode. So PineTS can be compared like for like with the Nautilus port on market-order strategies. Recorded boundary, fp-check TRUE POSITIVE: at tag commit c5e6b0ef, src/namespaces/strategy/utils.ts:331-345 fills entry 'stop' orders at order.stop whenever high>=stop (long) or low<=stop (short), with no clamp to the bar open. The stop-limit branch (line 357) uses Math.max(openPrice, order.stop), and the exit path (lines 1517-1518) documents TradingView's rule that an already-breached stop or limit fills at the next open. Slippage is then added to stop fills (line 400). This is the mechanism behind the seeded 34/85 out-of-range Bollinger stop fills, a count not re-measured here. The entry 'limit' branch (lines 314-327) has the same pattern; that is inferred from source and not measured. No issue or PR targeting entry-stop gap fills was found. The search covered the titles of the 30 most recently updated 'strategy' issues and PRs, plus a keyword grep of issue #316's body. The open items found are PR #367 (exit trailing stops), PR #389 (tick rounding), PR #393 (excursions), issue #316 (same-bar order processing, reversal sizing) and issue #274 (slippage on limit fills).
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Bounded native trial on linux-wsl2-x86_64, then macos-arm64. Freeze the T16 Pine strategies: RSI, MACD, Supertrend, Bollinger stop entry and one limit entry. Run PineTS 0.11.0 (npm pinets 0.11.0 at commit c5e6b0ef) offline through new PineTS(candles) on the retained 5-seed synthetic bars and the frozen SPY daily bars. Use two pre-registered semantics. (a) process_orders_on_close=true, compared with the NautilusTrader port under its default close settlement. (b) The default next-open semantics, compared only with PyneCore on the compiled upstream examples and with PineForge, because Nautilus has no native next-bar-open mode. Pass rule: identical trade lists (entry/exit bar, side, price, quantity at equal initial_capital) for market-order strategies, and every fill inside [low, high]. PineTS is overturned for a strategy class if any stop or limit entry fills outside [low, high], or a long stop fills below max(open, stop), in the release used, or if market-order trade-list identity with PyneCore or the matched Nautilus port is below 100%. It is then restricted to market-order strategies, or replaced for that class by the PineForge pair.

Orders pending from an earlier bar are processed before the script visit against the new bar's OHLC (host.py:3249-3252) at a gap-correct price (strategy_broker.py:530-542, strategy.py:2121-2133); this path is not a defect. counts.pin_status_note: pins_behind_upstream counts the generator's computed pin fields; pins_behind_upstream_by_review_status splits those rows by published review_status.
